game: SEA @ DEN, Week 6 2026, kickoff time not saved, DEN +2.5, total 40.5, outdoor Denver (altitude), weather not saved

script.base: Road favorite Seattle (-2.5, implied 21.5) and home dog Denver (implied 19.0) play a one-score, low-40s game. Seattle's points run through Jaxon Smith-Njigba as the air-yard hub (28 targets, 316 air yards in weeks 3-5) plus Emanuel Wilson on early downs with Zach Charbonnet out (50 carries / 156 yards). Denver's 19 points run through J.K. Dobbins (46 carries / 157 yards) and RJ Harvey's short targets (18 targets, -23 air). Starters finish; this is not a shootout and not a blowout.
script.flip1: Denver leads early at home. Seattle abandons the run, Wilson's carry line dies, and Sam Darnold funnels extra targets to Smith-Njigba, A.J. Barner and Cooper Kupp. Harvey's checkdowns can still live if Denver protects the lead with short throws while Dobbins keeps the rush share.
script.flip2: A slog, or unsaved Denver wind/cold, drags the total under 40.5 and both passing trees stall, so Wilson and Dobbins become the offense and the 94.5 and 22.5 receiving lines get squeezed. The other flip is the broken Denver secondary (Pat Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga out) turning Seattle's modest total into a Smith-Njigba spike.

That pass-defense hole lands first on Smith-Njigba, with spillover to Kupp, Rashid Shaheed and Barner. SEA LB Chazz Surratt Out (Calf) and Drake Thomas Out (Ankle): missing linebackers help Denver's TE/RB/slot group, chiefly Harvey (18 targets) and Evan Engram (11 targets), not the outside WRs. No offensive-line outs are listed. Sources: pack injury report and weeks 3-5 usage.

matchup.bleeds: Denver bleeds explosives and the run: 13 passes of 20+ for 174 yards, 4.91 rush YPC, 20 runs of 10+. Seattle does not: 8 passes of 20+, 3.83 rush YPC, 12 runs of 10+.
matchup.overlap: Primary overlap is Smith-Njigba, about 33% of Seattle targets (28 of 85) and 316 of the air yards, into a Denver secondary missing Surtain and Hufanga that already leaks the middle. Secondary overlap is Harvey's short-area receiving role into two missing Seattle linebackers, not into a statistically soft Seattle pass defense.

data_check.notes: No projection, no sims, and no Pinnacle print; model_p is the consensus no-vig fair, not an independent model, so the +3 point gate cannot be cleared and nothing is sized. Form agrees with both overs (Smith-Njigba 3 of 4 over 94.5; Harvey 3 of 4 over 22.5). The tension is script math: Seattle is only implied at 21.5, so 94.5 is a large share of that offense, and the market is still a coin flip after the known injuries. That disagreement flags the strong read for a human; it does not cut it. Wilson over 67.5 was considered from the Charbonnet outage and Denver's 4.91 YPC allowed, then left off because his own weeks 3-5 line is 52 yards a game. Treat any mental hit rate near 75% as uncalibrated.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost. Seattle grabbed an early lead in the altitude, Wilson (already a 16-carry back) ran the clock, and Darnold never needed a 95-yard Smith-Njigba day; the 76-yard game repeated inside a 21-point team total because the books had already moved 94.5 for Surtain. On the other side Dobbins stayed in, Seattle blitzed at its usual 21%, and Harvey posted the zero from his last four while Engram or Waddle took the middle. The coin-flip prices were the market telling us the injuries were known and the lines were not soft.
slip_story: One close-game, soft-spot story, not a shootout and not a clock-kill stack: Seattle concentrates on Smith-Njigba because Denver is missing Surtain and Hufanga, and Denver's modest dropback volume still feeds Harvey because Surratt and Thomas are out. Do not add Waddle or Sutton overs, a total over, or Wilson rush over 67.5 (same script, but 156 yards on 50 carries sits under the number). Two legs, one market per player, no touchdowns. Candidate read only; no bet placed.
